column3: Base function, used unchanged by the base's own schnorrsig_sign. Reported at -O0 only, with no report at -O2 or -Os on either base, which are the optimization levels a build ships. Its mask arithmetic is written to avoid branches, and gcc -O0 emits code memcheck reads as a jump on the undefined flag. The flag here is the parity of a secret-derived point. No claim about any other compiler or CPU.

The mutant writes one byte past t0, which changes no output, so a functional test can't catch it. Built with ASan, both sites report stack-buffer-overflow in the module tests and the unmutated build is clean: validation/c_module/run1_followup/h_asan.txt, benma base.

When ret is already 0 the output is zeroed or refused anyway. The cmov keeps zero and infinity out of the later arithmetic. The k' one also makes the self-check fail; see the pair experiments A2 and B2, where removing it alongside the |= mutant is caught.

Infinity becomes (0,0). No curve point has x = 0, since 7 is not a square mod p, so r = 0 fails BIP340 verification in step 5, and ECDSA refuses r = 0 on its own. The check stays because the specification requires it and the seam tests reach it.
Infinity becomes (0,0), so x(V) mod n = 0 can't equal r, which is refused at zero separately.

r = 0 then needs x(W) mod n = 0. x = 0 is on no curve point, so it needs x(W) = n, which needs a known discrete log and can't be produced in a test without forcing the group operation. The check stays because the text requires it.
s = 0 gives sinv = 0, so u1 = u2 = 0 and V at infinity, which the V check refuses.
k' = 0 can't produce a signature that passes the device's own host checks: BIP340 gets infinity, as above, and sig_sign fails for ECDSA. The check stays because the text requires it.
Only the branch with r >= p. schnorrsig_verify two lines later refuses r >= p and ANDs into ret unconditionally, so ret ends at 0 either way.

The call always returns 1 for a valid keypair, so |= would set ret to 1 after an earlier failure. The k' fallback then makes the signature disagree with the host check, which refuses. Pair experiment A2 removes that fallback as well and is caught, so the tests do see this if both barriers go.
Same reasoning as the BIP340 line. Pair experiment B2 removes the k' fallback as well and is caught.
A no-op unless the build defines VALGRIND. It tells the constant-time check that an output is public, and constant_time is where its absence shows. The Mull build doesn't define VALGRIND.

Four sites. L202 and L298 hold the k0 hash, a secret; L120 holds t, known to the device and secret from outside; L478 holds the challenge, public. A functional test can't see a clear, and residue's dead-memory scan didn't report these when removed, because later calls overwrite the same stack. They rest on the source and on the separate check that the wipes survive in the firmware build.
Hash of hc under a public tag, so derived from a value the host holds. Not found by the scan when removed. The clear stays by the module's rule of wiping intermediate values.
hc, pk32, pk33, r0 or xbuf. Public values, or derived from rho after its reveal. Not found by the scan when removed, and not secret.
